representative_collection.rationale: This is the smallest set that crosses all portability hazards the #6589 spine must exercise without duplicating a category: a reusable file capability (skill), an enforceable governance object (policy), sensitive state plus history (session), a live/checkpointed lifecycle (loop), and a harness/provider-specific environmental edge (model-binding). Receipt is transaction output rather than an input object; history, memory, checkpoint, lease, and credential-reference are dependency closure discovered while packaging these five. Removing any selected type drops one of file semantics, governance, sensitive continuity, active lifecycle, or environment binding.

objects.name: Session or loop recovery checkpoint
objects.identity_version: A session checkpoint is bound to a trace, parent/root hashes, and the fak session-image manifest; loop recovery positions are event-sequence and registry-state based.
objects.lifecycle: created at an explicit boundary, verified, restored or forked, then retained or garbage-collected with its parent state
objects.export: Session-image directories and archives carry checkpoint state; loop checkpoint position has no standalone export.
objects.import: Session image load/rehydrate accepts the session half; no common checkpoint importer spans session and loop state.
objects.sync: No unified sync; callers move session archives while loop event ledgers remain workspace-local.
objects.gap: Unify checkpoint identity and dependency closure across session images and active loop ledgers.

objects.name: Credential and account-home reference
objects.identity_version: Registry schema fak-config-homes/v1; identity is disk-derived account metadata plus non-secret fingerprints or environment-variable names, never credential bytes.
objects.lifecycle: discover or enroll, reconcile, activate, cool down, tombstone, and rehome
objects.export: Registry dumps can describe homes and references but deliberately exclude live tokens and keys.
objects.import: Registry/config-home adoption exists, but secret provisioning remains an out-of-band local action.
objects.sync: Generated roster views synchronize non-secret metadata; credentials themselves do not sync.
objects.gap: Define a portable unresolved-reference form and a destination-side credential rebind ceremony without serializing secrets.

objects.name: Harness process profile and adapter selection
objects.identity_version: Canonical profile name plus detect aliases; the JSON override vocabulary is closed over wire, repoint mechanism, credential kind, and identity reader.
objects.lifecycle: built in or declared, validated, merged over defaults, selected at launch, and reset at process teardown
objects.export: Built-ins can be inspected in code and resolved profiles can be dumped by callers; there is no canonical portable profile artifact.
objects.import: Strict JSON overrides load and merge, but they can only reference adapters shipped by the destination binary.
objects.sync: No profile sync or conflict protocol.
objects.gap: Package a versioned profile with adapter compatibility and a secret-free destination resolution report.

objects.name: Conversation and session hash history
objects.identity_version: Trace heads point into a SHA-256 parent-linked entry DAG; bounded content may be replaced with a byte-count and digest provenance stub.
objects.lifecycle: append, fork, checkpoint, rewind, rotate or elide, export closure, and import closure
objects.export: fak session export writes the selected trace hash closure.
objects.import: fak session import verifies and merges a portable closure into the destination ledger.
objects.sync: Manual archive movement is supported; there is no continuous reconciliation protocol.
objects.gap: Add redaction policy, conflict explanation, and incremental/offline synchronization around the existing closure format.

objects.name: Ownership and concurrency lease
objects.identity_version: Lease ID plus holder, tree globs, TTL, session ID, and monotonic fencing generation; git object identity protects ref payloads.
objects.lifecycle: acquire, renew, fence, expire, reap, release, and rehydrate
objects.export: Git refs expose records to a clone without a separate bundle format.
objects.import: Fetching refs makes records visible; admission still validates expiry, holder, session liveness, and generation.
objects.sync: Git ref push/fetch provides cross-machine visibility, not globally atomic acquisition.
objects.gap: Separate portable intent/liveness evidence from host-local holders and define collision-safe reconciliation.

objects.name: Durable recurring work loop
objects.identity_version: Registry schema fak.loop-registry.v1 keyed by job/loop ID; append-only events use fak.loop-event.v1 and a monotonic sequence.
objects.lifecycle: register, arm, fire, admit or refuse, end, pause, drain, recover, rotate, and retire
objects.export: Definitions are reviewable JSON; live event/checkpoint state has reports but no complete portable export.
objects.import: Registry JSON loads strictly; there is no atomic import of active state, leases, and pending work.
objects.sync: Fleet rollups read multiple ledgers, but active state is not reconciled between hosts.
objects.gap: Checkpoint and quiesce the process/lease/event closure before moving an active loop, then rebind host capabilities.

objects.name: Canonical memory page and derived memory view
objects.scope: session, agent, or user knowledge view
objects.identity_version: Raw pages are content-addressed; a derived view binds view ID, producer version, source digest/span, taint, freshness epoch, witness, and invalidation rule.
objects.lifecycle: ingest, index, materialize, invalidate or recompute, quarantine, retain, and forget
objects.export: Session images can carry recall pages and views; memory inspection emits formats, but no whole memory-space export contract exists.
objects.import: Session rehydrate restores image-backed memory; loose harness memory roots are only scanned/reconciled locally.
objects.sync: No cross-root merge, precedence, deletion, or conflict protocol.
objects.gap: Define typed raw/view dependency closure, sensitivity-aware redaction, and deterministic merge/delete semantics.

objects.name: Model/provider route and account binding
objects.scope: organization, workspace, task, request, or tool call
objects.identity_version: Route manifests use fak-route/v1; model bindings identify model, provider/account reference, aspect, reduction, and policy provenance rather than credential bytes.
objects.lifecycle: declare, validate, resolve, route, degrade or fail closed, audit, and retire
objects.export: Versioned manifests and non-secret rosters can be dumped or copied.
objects.import: Strict loaders accept manifests/rosters when referenced providers, models, and account handles exist.
objects.sync: No common sync; fleet/config generation moves selected views while availability remains host-local.
objects.gap: Resolve destination capabilities and credential references explicitly, preserving an unsupported/degraded report.

objects.name: Orchestration and execution plan
objects.identity_version: Workflow plans use fak-orchestration-plan/1 and carry task ID, roles, DAG, budgets, leases, witness policy, engine reference, degradations, and explanation.
objects.lifecycle: resolve from task/profile, validate, approve, execute, reconcile, supersede, and archive
objects.export: Resolved plans are stable JSON values and can be rendered by callers.
objects.import: The package parses resolutions, but no unified activation command installs a plan across harnesses.
objects.sync: No plan sync; shared-task and fleet surfaces exchange narrower projections.
objects.gap: Give stored plans stable provenance and adapter compatibility, then bind activation/reconciliation to one transaction.

objects.name: Capability and organization policy
objects.scope: built-in, organization, workspace, session, or tool
objects.identity_version: Strict versioned manifests and optional signed organization envelopes; precedence and amendments retain policy/version provenance.
objects.lifecycle: author or dump, validate, sign/pull, compose by precedence, activate, amend, audit, and revoke
objects.export: fak policy --dump and manifest files provide deterministic portable bytes; signed envelopes preserve issuer provenance.
objects.import: fak policy --check and runtime loaders validate before activation and fail closed on unknown structure.
objects.sync: Organization pull exists, but general personal/team/public channel reconciliation is not unified.
objects.gap: Attach dependencies, target compatibility, channel trust, and conflict/rollback receipts to otherwise portable policy bytes.

objects.name: Tool, audit, and transaction evidence receipt
objects.scope: tool call, session, task, audit, or transaction
objects.identity_version: Receipt families use explicit schema/version fields and commonly bind subject, policy, model/tool result, hashes, sequence, and independent witness evidence.
objects.lifecycle: emit, append/hash-chain, verify, fold, retain, redact, and expire
objects.export: Several receipt families are JSON/JSONL and independently verifiable; there is no common envelope for all families.
objects.import: Family-specific verifiers load receipts; importing one does not recreate the underlying effect.
objects.sync: Ledgers may be copied or mirrored by their owner, without one receipt reconciliation policy.
objects.gap: Define a common typed envelope, sensitivity rules, and effect/reference semantics for package/apply/rollback receipts.

objects.name: Managed agent session and portable session image
objects.scope: agent process, user, workspace, and optional fleet
objects.identity_version: Stable session/trace ID plus durable descriptor generation and heartbeat; session images use a versioned integrity manifest over drive, recall, trajectory, and metadata parts.
objects.lifecycle: create, register/heartbeat, run, compact, checkpoint, fork, snapshot, export/import, rehydrate, end, quarantine, and reap
objects.export: Session images and fak session export/archive carry a verified state closure.
objects.import: Session image load/rehydrate and fak session import restore durable data into a destination ledger.
objects.sync: Session descriptors can publish through git refs, but live process, provider, and local harness state are not atomically synchronized.
objects.gap: Separate portable state from host/process bindings, redact sensitive content, and transact activation with rollback.

objects.name: Agent skill capability
objects.scope: agent, project, user, plugin, or installation
objects.identity_version: Capability reference kind=skill plus frontmatter name/version; SHA-256 of complete SKILL.md bytes is the content identity.
objects.lifecycle: discover, index frontmatter, fault body on demand, invoke, measure, update, deprecate, and remove
objects.export: A skill directory is file-portable and content-addressable, but there is no canonical dependency/redaction package command.
objects.import: Placement under a recognized skill root makes it discoverable; harness-specific frontmatter and tool assumptions may degrade.
objects.sync: External repository/plugin mechanisms may move files; fak has no precedence/conflict/revocation sync contract.
objects.gap: Package license/provenance, tool dependencies, scope/precedence, sensitivity, and harness compatibility with the SKILL.md bytes.

objects.name: Shared or managed task record
objects.identity_version: fak.shared-task.v1 task IDs with versioned event, patch, patch-result, artifact-reference, and task-journal schemas.
objects.lifecycle: create, assign, patch, approve/refuse, execute, record events/artifacts, reconcile conflicts, close, and archive
objects.export: Versioned JSON schemas and examples provide portable task/event records.
objects.import: Strict contract validation accepts records, but activation into every scheduler/harness is adapter-specific.
objects.sync: Journals and patches support exchange; there is no universal channel or precedence/conflict controller.
objects.gap: Bind task records to portable plans, artifacts, identities, and destination scheduler capabilities.

objects.name: Tool definition, runtime binding, and capability grant
objects.scope: harness, session, agent, model request, and policy
objects.identity_version: Tool definitions carry names and JSON schemas while runtime calls/grants bind operation, arguments, engine, scope, and policy; no single cross-surface binding ID/version exists.
objects.lifecycle: declare/discover, adapt to a provider wire, grant, bind, invoke, adjudicate, record receipt, revoke, and unload
objects.export: Catalog/tool schemas can be emitted by individual surfaces; runtime handlers and capability grants are not serializable as one object.
objects.import: MCP/catalog and policy loaders ingest subsets; executable binding remains destination code/process state.
objects.sync: No common sync, identity, or compatibility negotiation across harness and MCP/provider adapters.
objects.gap: Choose the stable object boundary between declarative tool schema, executable handler, grant, and model-wire adapter before claiming portability.

objects.name: Agent trajectory corpus
objects.identity_version: Typed per-turn records with stable JSONL export; ATIF export uses the Agent Trajectory Interchange Format profile and source/provenance fields.
objects.lifecycle: record, scrub, export, import JSONL, mine/cluster, attach to image, retain, and delete
objects.export: fak traj export writes deterministic JSONL or ATIF trajectory.json.
objects.import: The recorder imports fak JSONL and scrubbed chat; ATIF is export-only today.
objects.sync: No continuous sync; corpora are moved as files or inside session images.
objects.gap: Add ATIF import/round-trip, redaction classification, and referenced artifact/tool/model dependency closure.

objects.name: Multi-agent workflow definition and resolution
objects.identity_version: Resolution schema fak-orchestration-plan/1 plus profile name, task ID, role/DAG topology, budgets, witness and reconciliation policy, engine reference, and degradations.
objects.lifecycle: declare profile, resolve against task and harness capabilities, validate/degrade, launch roles, reconcile, and finish
objects.export: Resolution values serialize deterministically; no user-facing workflow package/export surface owns dependencies.
objects.import: ParseResolution loads the typed value, while launch semantics still depend on destination harness capabilities.
objects.sync: No workflow registry/sync or active-role state transfer.
objects.gap: Package role prompts, skills, tools, model bindings, leases, and degradation policy with harness conformance evidence.
